[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended potting soil for herbs should be well-draining, have good aeration, have a neutral to slightly acidic pH, contain organic matter, and have a balanced fertilizer.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided tips for choosing potting soil for herbs, including looking for mixes designed for herbs or vegetables and avoiding overly nitrogen-rich soils.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant listed popular potting soil brands for herbs: Miracle-Gro Organic Choice Herb & Vegetable Garden Soil, Espoma Organic Herb & Vegetable Garden Soil, Black Kow All Purpose Potting Mix, E.B. Stone Organics Herb & Vegetable Garden Soil.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested a DIY potting mix recipe: 2 parts peat moss or coconut coir, 1 part vermiculite or perlite, 1 part compost or worm castings, 1 part well-rotted manure or aged chicken manure.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant advised on fertilization, suggesting a balanced, water-soluble fertilizer specifically formulated for herbs to promote healthy growth.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided specific fertilizer recommendations: Miracle-Gro Organic Choice Herb & Vegetable Plant Food, Espoma Organic Indoor! Herb & Vegetable Plant Food, E.B. Stone Organics Bloom! Herb & Vegetable Fertilizer.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant outlined when to fertilize herbs, including starting 1-2 weeks after planting and fertilizing every 1-2 weeks during the growing season.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided pruning tips for mint, cilantro, and parsley, including pinching off flower buds, harvesting regularly, and using clean tools.
